# Python-Markdown Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to the
[Python Version Specification](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/version-specifiers/).
See the [Contributing Guide](contributing.md) for details.

## [Unreleased]

### Fixed

* Support automatic links with URL schemes other than HTTP and FTP, such as
  `<ssh://example.org>` (#1244).
* Fix quadratic-time id generation in the `toc` extension when many headers
  share the same text.
* Ignore glossary abbreviations with empty definitions after inline elements,
  consistently with abbreviations before inline elements.
* Strip complete HTML tags with quoted `>` characters from `toc` labels and
  generated heading IDs.
* Fix quadratic-time regex backtracking in `attr_list` when a block ends with an
  unclosed attribute list followed by a long run of spaces, e.g. a line
  consisting only of `{` and some text with many trailing spaces (#1656).
* Fix quadratic-time regex backtracking in hash headers when a long run of `#`

findings.problem: There's no changelog entry. docs/contributing.md (lines 535-540) says every change to code behavior needs an entry under `[Unreleased]` in docs/changelog.md. Every other recent fix on this branch adds one under `### Fixed`. This PR changes how `toc` behaves and adds nothing there.
findings.evidence: `git diff HEAD~1 --stat` touches only markdown/extensions/toc.py and tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_toc.py. The contributing guide says: 'any way must include an entry in the changelog... The current changelog can be found at `docs/changelog.md`.'

findings.problem: The new test class docstring cites issue `#1705`, but the PR closes issue #1. That reference looks wrong or made up. It should point to the actual issue, or be dropped.
findings.evidence: The docstring reads "The `toc` extension together with `attr_list` (#1705)." The PR description says 'Closes #1'.

findings.problem: The check `not el.attrib.get("id")` also catches an explicit empty id like `{id=""}`. Before, an empty id was kept, which gave an `href="#"` TOC link. Now a slug replaces it. That part is out of scope, but worth a follow-up issue.
